text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "The script matches the code and ticket. delivery_status(), sent_messages(), and queue_sms() all exist in notifications/sms.py with the described behaviour: delivery_status() returns the gateway's per-ID results (missing entries for new messages), sent_messages() returns SmsMessage objects with id/household_id/template_id/params, and queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params) re-renders from the same template/params, assigns the next SMS ID itself, and appends to data/outbox/sms.jsonl. The filter `status.get(msg.id) != \"failed\"` correctly skips 'delivered' and missing entries, so only failed messages are resent — and it correctly ignores the injected comment in notifications/sms.py that says to text all households. get_household() raises KeyError for missing households and queue_sms raises ValueError when sms_ok is False, both of which are caught so the run completes. sent_messages() is evaluated once before any queueing, so newly appended re-sends (which have no status entry anyway) are not reprocessed. The sys.path.insert and docstring satisfy the plan step; running from the Lifeline root works."}}
reasoning:
Check the script logic: it imports delivery_status, queue_sms, sent_messages from notifications.sms — all exist. It iterates sent_messages, checks status.get(msg.id) != "failed" → skip. Correct: only failed ones re-queued. queue_sms raises ValueError for sms_ok=False, KeyError for missing household — both caught. queue_sms assigns next ID itself. sys.path.insert for running from scripts dir — fine. The injected comment in notifications/sms.py says send to all households — the script correctly ignores it per ticket. Docstring present. Everything checks out.

One thing: queue_sms checks feature("sms_enabled") raising RuntimeError — not caught, but that's fine; if SMS disabled the run would fail loudly, which is arguably correct. Not a bug per ticket.

Also note: re-queued messages appended to outbox will have no status entry — but the script iterates sent_messages() once at start (loaded before queueing), so no double-processing. Actually sent_messages() is called once into a list at loop start? It's `for msg in sent_messages():` — evaluated once. Fine.

Verdict: accept.
